activities.activity: Working a night shift as an aged-care support worker, doing routine resident checks, personal care assistance and medication prompts in a residential care facility
Commuting home after the night shift by train and bus from the care facility to Clayton
Eating a quiet light breakfast of toast and fruit with a cup of tea and rinsing the dishes straight away so the kitchen stays clear
Taking a warm shower and changing out of work clothes after the night shift
Setting up for daytime sleep: turning on the fan for white noise, closing the curtains, silencing the phone and checking the written reminder list for later in the day
Sleeping after the night shift in a quiet, dark room with the fan running
Waking slowly, drinking a cup of tea, rereading written reminders and checking text messages for confirmed plans
Shopping for groceries on foot and by bus, paying in cash and sticking to the weekly budget list
Cooking a flexitarian dinner of rice, lentils and stir-fried vegetables using the rice cooker and induction cooker
Eating dinner at the table with a pot of tea and writing out the next day's written to-do list
Washing the dishes, wiping down the bench and putting away the dry goods from the grocery run
Doing a load of laundry in the washing machine and drying the clothes in the dryer
Studying at the desk on the computer, reading required social work course readings and taking detailed notes
Making another cup of tea and taking a short break from study
Drafting a written assignment on the computer with the desk lamp on, checking the marking rubric point by point
Reviewing the weekly budget, counting cash set aside for rent and bills and updating the paper spending record
Evening wash, brushing teeth and preparing for bed
Winding down in bed with the fan on, reading quietly until falling asleep
